opening: horror. good. let's find you something.

questions.ask: first though, how much of you is actually watching this?

options.say: honestly? it's just noise. I'm doing something else.
options.reply: fair enough. easy company, nothing that needs following.

options.say: I'll be half in. looking up when something happens.
options.reply: the classic. half a film is still a film.

options.say: I want to disappear into it and forget the world exists.
options.reply: now we're talking. I'll bring you the good stuff.
options.note: a rating floor is defensible here and nowhere else: the viewer has explicitly asked for something worth disappearing into, so filtering on quality is answering them rather than overruling them.

questions.ask: so what scares you the most?

options.say: I don't care. anything scary. I'm easy.
I'm not really scared unless it's supernatural.
options.reply: ghosts and demons then. things that shouldn't be there.

options.say: psycho killers. people are the scariest thing there is.
options.reply: agreed, frankly. no ghost ever followed anyone home.

options.say: something with teeth. a monster, a creature, a thing.
options.reply: good. monsters are honest about what they want.

options.say: the slow kind. the sort that gets under your skin and stays.
options.reply: the ones that ruin the drive home. I know the type.

options.say: make me laugh while I'm scared.
options.reply: nothing wrong with a film that knows it's ridiculous.

options.say: shaky camera, someone found the tapes.
options.reply: brave. half of these are terrible and you know it.

questions.ask: alright. how much blood can you actually take?

options.reply: noted. nothing you'll have to look away from.
options.pail: spotless, sparkling, not a mark on it

options.say: some. I'll look away when I need to.
options.pail: splattered down one side, blood pooling in the bottom
nearly full, first drops hitting the floor
a chum bucket standing in a spreading pool

questions.note: Four pails on the genome gore scale plus TMDB gore keywords (decision 59), cut at the reference's 40th, 70th and 90th percentiles. A film with no genome entry appears only under 'some' and 'properly messy' unless a house pin places it. A viewer excluding any listed blood or gore topic is never asked and is treated as 'none'.

questions.ask: still plenty to choose from. does era matter?

options.say: give me something old. eighties, nineties.
options.reply: practical effects and no phones. nice.

questions.ask: last one. do you mind walking into the middle of a franchise?

options.say: no sequels. I don't want homework.
I don't care, I'll work it out.

human_killer.note: chainsaw, murder and mask were removed after Gremlins and Army of Darkness both matched on chainsaw alone. murder appears on 93 of 599 horror titles and names nothing useful.

funny.note: the Comedy genre tag beats any keyword cluster here. Measured against 599 horror titles: the tag found 114, the keyword cluster 64, and the tag caught 80 the keywords missed including Tucker and Dale, Happy Death Day, Army of Darkness and Cabin in the Woods. Genre tags are reliable for co-membership and unreliable only as a primary label. See discussion log 17.

found_footage.note: no genome equivalent: 'found footage' is not in the 1,128-tag vocabulary

creeping.note: derived from what the target films share rather than from a word meaning dread. Half of them carry no dread keyword at all: Get Out, Poltergeist, 1408 and Oculus carry none. What they do share is a haunted place or a psychological frame. The gore ceiling was removed: blood is already its own question and gating creeping on it wrongly excluded Get Out, Weapons and The Babadook. See discussion log 11.

genome.source: MovieLens ml-latest, generated 2023-07-20, joined on TMDB id via its links.csv
genome.note: A film joins a flavour when its genome relevance reaches the threshold OR its keywords match, not one as a fallback for the other. Measured across 27 fixtures: genome alone passes 21 to 25 depending on threshold; the union passes 27 at every threshold from 0.45 to 0.60, and cuts films matching no flavour from 73 to 44. The two signals fail on different films, so keeping both is strictly better than choosing between them.
